The still shore of a glassy woodland lake, water-lilies drifting across faintly luminous water, the entire canopy reflected without a ripple, a weeping willow trailing silver fingers into its own perfect mirror image below.

A glass-clear rill threading between primrose-scattered banks, smooth moss-packed stepping stones crossing the shallows, birch trees leaning tenderly over the current to watch their own pale reflections waver and settle.

A fern-curtained waterfall pool, soft perpetual spray catching a single shaft of sunlight into brief scattered gold, boulders wearing jewel-bright emerald moss, the pool surface trembling with the gentlest possible breath of falling water.
A wildflower meadow foaming with red poppies and deep cornflowers, a glassy pool lying still at its heart like a dropped mirror, ancient oaks standing in great dark arches at the meadow's far edge.

A quietly welling spring spreading outward across a carpet of deep luminous moss, its surface mirror-still and faintly glowing, ancient yews encircling it with cathedral silence, roots silvered where they dip into the cold bright water.

A silver rill threading through a blossom grove, fallen petals lying knee-deep in drifts of white and palest rose, the current carrying single blooms downstream like tiny paper boats between moss-velvet banks.

A small clearing pool perfectly round and glassy, reflecting an unbroken circle of sky ringed by ancient oaks, water-crowfoot blossoms floating white across the luminous surface, moss banks glowing soft emerald at every edge.

A glass-clear woodland stream rushing over amber pebbles, foxgloves crowding the banks in tall pink spires, stepping stones crossing the brightest shallows, a canopy of ash and hazel arching overhead in tender protective curves.

A deep waterfall pool veiled behind curtains of hanging fern, spray drifting in slow perpetual clouds, sunlight occasionally piercing the green canopy to ignite the mist into threads of suspended gold above wet glowing boulders.

A poppy-and-cornflower meadow blazing at midsummer, a shallow rill threading its heart in bright silver loops, old hawthorns foaming with late white blossom along the far tree-line, their reflections trembling in the water below.

A still woodland lake at the edge of deep forest, its faintly luminous surface holding a perfect inverted canopy of oak and beech, a single willow leaning to press its reflection gently into the glassy dark water.

A moss-banked stream turning a slow wide bend, forget-me-nots and celandines foaming along every edge, ancient alders leaning from both banks until their topmost branches very nearly touch above the running silver water.

A spring welling silently from beneath a great moss-covered root, spreading in a mirror-still luminous sheet across deep green moss, the surrounding forest pressing close in quiet attendance, bluebells rising from the moss in violet drifts.

A blossom grove in full surrender to spring, petals heaped knee-deep against every root and hollow, a bright silver rill running through it all unhurried, carrying loose petals on its surface far into the deeper forest.

A waterfall stepping down three shallow mossy ledges into a clear pool, spray catching every wandering sunbeam into momentary prismatic fire, hart's-tongue ferns draping the wet rock face in overlapping tongues of vivid green.

A sun-warmed woodland glade with a shallow pool at its centre, water so clear the sandy bottom glows amber-gold, ragged-robin and meadowsweet crowding the banks, old oaks framing the glade in their great patient arms.

A glass-clear brook running over smooth white stones between banks thick with primroses, silver birches standing in pairs along its length, each trunk reflected in the current as a trembling column of pale light.

A wildflower clearing where cornflowers and ox-eye daisies grow waist-deep, a glassy pool occupying the lowest hollow at its centre, the open sky reflected perfectly within it, dark ancient oaks framing every horizon.

A fern-curtained waterfall pool in deep forest shadow, the water faintly luminous beneath the surface, boulders bearded with moss so green it seems lit from within, spray hanging in the air like permanent fine rain.

A long glassy lake running deep into the forest, its far shore lost in soft mist, ancient beeches marching along both banks, their copper canopy reflected so perfectly the water and the trees seem to breathe together.

A mossy spring rising silently through pale gravel into a wide still basin, the water spreading luminous and barely rippled, wild garlic flowering white at every edge, ash trees standing in a protective ring overhead.

A shallow ford where a silver rill threads a drift of primroses and wood anemones, stepping stones green with age and padded moss, hazels on both banks arching low enough that their catkins brush the bright current.

A hidden waterfall pool enclosed by ancient rowan trees, red berries reflected doubled in the still water, spray settling as fine dew on every surrounding leaf and fern, the pool glowing with its own faint inner light.

A midsummer meadow of poppies running to the edge of old forest, a threading rill catching flecks of red reflected light as it threads the open ground, entering the oak-shadow in a bright unhurried silver ribbon.

A glassy forest lake ringed entirely by ancient willows, each tree trailing its branches into its own reflection, water-lilies resting motionless on the luminous surface, the whole scene enclosed in green arching silence and soft gold light.
